{"url": "https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search?query=autonomous+agent+methods+for+prioritizing+novel+research+problems&format=json&resultType=core&pageSize=4", "scope": "Europe PMC search metadata, abstracts and full-text links; discovery only", "excerpt": "[{\"title\": \"Closing the Empirical Loop: Autonomous AI Agents Conduct End-to-end Research With Human Participants.\", \"abstract\": \"Artificial intelligence systems are transforming scientific discovery by accelerating specific research tasks, from protein structure prediction to materials design, yet remain confined to narrow domains requiring substantial human oversight. Exponential growth of scientific literature and increasing domain specialization constrain researchers' capacity to synthesize knowledge across disciplines and develop unifying theories, motivating exploration of general-purpose AI systems for science. Here we show that a domain-agnostic, agentic AI Scientist system can independently navigate the scientific workflow -from hypothesis generation through data collection to manuscript preparation. The system autonomously designed and executed three psychological studies on visual working memory, mental rotation, and imagery vividness, executed online data collection with 288 participants, developed analysis pipelines through 8h+ continuous coding sessions, and produced completed manuscripts. The results demonstrate the capability of AI scientific discovery pipelines to conduct research with theoretical reasoning and methodological rigor comparable to experienced researchers, though with limitations in conceptual nuance and theoretical interpretation. This is a step toward embodied AI that can test hypotheses through real-world experiments, accelerating discovery by autonomously exploring regions of scientific space that human cognitive and resource constraints might otherwise leave unexplored. See [the reusable kernel contract](kernel.md) for application ownership and the
non-research execution proof, and [installation boundaries](installations.md) for
independent records and runtime lifecycles. These remain inside this repository.

The local [improvement application](improvements.md) uses that same kernel contract
in an explicitly new experiment record. Captured public research informs code
proposals; it does not become writable research authority. Untrusted candidate
code runs only in restricted disposable containers, while the host scores its
outputs. An operator review receipt cannot apply code or grant release authority.

The [autonomous context lane](autonomous-context.md) is a separate WAKE application
policy on the existing per-node native authority. An installed capability permits
one selector-field change, gated by recomputed fixed-task and current-native-state
measurements. Proposal generation, adoption and rollback require no per-change
human review. Metadata events preserve research versions and history; candidate
data cannot replace the evaluator, widen permissions, modify code or create a
competing research store. Native replay owns the policy after restart.

> **Current specification.** This document explains why the present system is shaped this way: its trust boundary, durable record, governance model and known limits. Current local procedures belong in `standalone.md`; public mirror publishing belongs in `cloud.md`. Maintainer navigation, environment checks and reproducible validation guidance belong in `development.md`.

**WAKE✳︎** is infrastructure for continuity of accountable work, not continuity of a model instance. Its stable sequence is **Record → Context → Proposal → Governance → Transition → Receipt**.
